Handshake order, host side (orchestra/core/src/link/conn.rs:248-325): (1) WebSocket upgrade; /link always, /pair only while a window is open, otherwise plain HTTP 404 (conn.rs:196-215). (2) client sends ONE TEXT frame {"proto":"orchestra","v":1} (codec.rs:277-279 encode_handshake_request); host replies ONE TEXT frame (conn.rs:255-262; reply shape codec.rs:293-305). Client text frames are read only if at most 1024 bytes (conn.rs:36, conn.rs:88-100). (3) client sends Noise message 1 as one BINARY frame. (4) host sends Noise message 2 as one BINARY frame (conn.rs send_raw Message::binary). (5) client sends first transport message as BINARY: the encrypted hello.

Payloads inside the Noise handshake: none. Both sides write an empty payload (test client orchestra/core/tests/link_support/mod.rs:238-250 and 253-264 use hs.write(&[]); host conn.rs writes hs.write(&[]) for message 2). Pairing: the client static key is carried encrypted inside IKpsk2 message 1 (noise.rs:98-110; host learns it via remote_static, conn.rs handshake). Reconnect: no key in KK message 1; host tries each stored client key, at most 32 (noise.rs:117-135, clients.rs:17 MAX_CLIENTS=32). The client name is NOT in the handshake: it rides in the first transport message, hello.

Hello: encrypted JSON {v:1, type:"hello", client_name, app_version} (orchestra/protocol/types.ts:158; host decode in orchestra/core/src/wire/codec.rs). Anything but hello first closes the socket; on /link a bad_request error is sent first (conn.rs handshake(), the non-hello arm). A non-hello on /pair closes silently. Host input is strict: unknown fields are bad_request (protocol/README.md, What P2 decided, Tolerance).

Pairing confirmation: after hello the host holds the connection and calls on_pairing_request (conn.rs:344-381, name clipped by clip()); confirm_timeout = 300 s (orchestra/core/src/link/mod.rs:59). Only after confirm does the host send welcome. Default scopes read+answer (orchestra/core/src/link/clients.rs:19). Reconnect (/link): welcome is sent straight after hello (conn.rs:383-420 run()).

Framing (orchestra/core/src/link/frame.rs): one application message = one WebSocket BINARY message holding a run of [u16 big-endian length][Noise ciphertext] chunks. Max plaintext per chunk MAX_CHUNK = 65519 (frame.rs:10-11; noise.rs:21-24 MAX_NOISE_MESSAGE=65535, TAG_BYTES=16). seal() frame.rs:50-66: empty message = one empty chunk. open() frame.rs:70-93 refuses when joined plaintext would pass the cap, before decrypting the overflowing chunk. Cap MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4194304 (orchestra/protocol/constants.ts:11; same in core wire). WebSocket-layer cap = frame::max_wire_bytes(4 MiB) = 65 chunks x 65537 = 4259905 bytes (frame.rs:44-47; applied conn.rs upgrade() lines 206-208).

Binary vs text after the handshake: every post-handshake message is BINARY (conn.rs wait(binary=true) lines 88-100; send() lines 107-115 uses Message::binary). A TEXT frame after the handshake makes the host close (conn.rs run(): Polled::Text or Closed breaks the loop). No subprotocol or header is required: the accept callback checks only the path (conn.rs:204-215); no Origin or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol check.

Timeouts and keepalive (orchestra/core/src/link/mod.rs:52-60): handshake_timeout 10 s (covers the version exchange too), write_timeout 30 s, idle_timeout 120 s measured from the last BINARY frame received (conn.rs run(): last_rx is updated only in the Binary arm). Client must send type ping within 60 s (mod.rs:37); host answers type pong (conn.rs handle_binary). The host sends no keepalive of its own. Also 16 connections (mod.rs:52), 10 handshakes per minute per source (mod.rs:53; server.rs:456), 8 calls in flight per connection (mod.rs:54).

After the handshake the host sends, in this order (conn.rs run(), about lines 383-420): welcome {v,type:welcome,host_id,host_name,scopes,features:[]} (types.ts:167-173); snapshot {v,type:snapshot,seq,projects,sessions,inbox,tasks,storage} only if the client holds read (types.ts:175-183); then event {v,type:event,seq,name,payload} per published event to read-scope clients (types.ts:185-190); result {v,type:result,id,ok or error} (types.ts:194-195); pong; error {v,type:error,code,message,supported?} (types.ts:196-202). There is NO subscribe message: the subscription is implicit at connect (protocol METHODS, orchestra/protocol/constants.ts:19-35, has no subscribe).

Seq: one process-wide counter, assigned in publish order. snapshot.seq = seq of the last event the snapshot reflects; the first later event = snapshot.seq + 1 (protocol/README.md, What P3 decided, Snapshot and events). Core test orchestra/core/src/session/mod.rs:2959-2971 asserts view.seq equals the event count. Subscribe is atomic with the snapshot (orchestra/core/src/session/mod.rs:682-692). Per-connection queue 1024 events (mod.rs:55 in link); overflow closes the socket (conn.rs run(), TryRecvError::Disconnected arm). v1 has no replay: a seq gap means reconnect for a fresh snapshot.

decisions_for_gate.recommend: A fresh client static key per paired host, generated at pairing (hosts cannot correlate the phone, and forgetting one host deletes exactly its key). decisions_for_gate.topic: What a silent close means (amends README Revocation)
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Track the phase reached. (1) The WebSocket never opens: unreachable; on /pair a close reason containing 404 = code used or window closed. (2) An error frame in the version exchange: version mismatch, definitive. (3) /link closed after msg1 without msg2: after 2 in a row with the network up, show Not paired with this host, with Pair again / Forget this desktop, and keep retrying at the slow backoff. (4) /pair msg2 fails to decrypt: wrong code or host key, definitive for that QR. (5) /pair closed after hello, before welcome: rejected, timed out or desktop stopped (the phone cannot tell which). (6) error revoked: Removed from <host>. Pair again., and delete that host record and key. Keys are deleted automatically only on revoked, or on Forget. The s1 README section amends the Revocation line that says the phone deletes its keys on a failed handshake.
alternatives: Follow the README literally (delete keys on the first failed /link handshake): one dropped packet or a desktop restart unpairs the phone. Not recommended.
Never auto-delete, even on revoked: leaves a dead key in storage. Not recommended.

decisions_for_gate.recommend: Ping every 25 s after welcome; if no pong or other host message arrives within 15 s of a ping, close and reconnect. Backoff 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 30 s capped, with up to 20% jitter (Math.random allowed for jitter only, banned in the crypto files); that stays under the host limit of 10 handshakes a minute per source. Each attempt tries the stored addrs in order with a 5 s connect timeout each. Reset the backoff and try at once when expo-network reports connectivity regained or AppState becomes active; no attempts while offline. A seq gap, a decrypt failure, a TEXT frame after the handshake or an undecodable message closes and reconnects at once (once; repeats back off). The socket is left alone in the background; if Android kills it, the foreground reconnect covers it, which keeps the door open for the A3 recently-backgrounded notifications.
alternatives: Close on background and reopen on foreground: simpler, but A3 would undo it.
A host-side keepalive: a core change for no A1 need. No.

So in any dev bundle, including npx expo start --go (the G4 owner check, the only way A1 reaches a phone), random(32) yields Math.random bytes for the per-host client static key that the desktop stores and trusts, and for Noise ephemerals once s4 wires it. saveHost and forgetHost read-modify-write orchestra.hosts with no serialization; a concurrent save of A and forget of B can drop A from the index, orphaning its record and client_secret_key in SecureStore. A crash between the record write and the index write also leaves an orphan secret nothing deletes (ignored per G5, never cleaned). Serialize store calls in s4/s5 or sweep orphans.

Only JSON.parse failure is treated as absent. SecureStore.getItemAsync can itself throw (Android keystore decrypt failure after a lock-screen change, or an invalid key name from a corrupted index entry, since readIndex keeps any string), and listHosts then rejects outright. s4/s5 callers must catch it.

Octets with leading zeros (192.168.001.020) are accepted; WHATWG-style URL parsers read them as octal. The host never emits them (Rust SocketAddr Display), and a crafted QR can point anywhere anyway. host_name is unbounded here and caught only by the 2048-byte assert in saveHost; s4 should clip it or handle that throw.

findings.issue: dispose() while pair() is in flight, with a host already stored (the not_paired -> Pair again flow), leaks a live controller. dispose bumps epoch and closes the pair socket; pair() then sees the epoch mismatch and calls finish({Closed}), and finish calls this.attempt() because this.record is set. attempt reads the NEW epoch, so runAttempt passes every epoch check. On /pair a silent close after msg1 maps to Unreachable. conn.rs closes there when the QR host key does not match the host at that address (hs.read fails) or the window closed between upgrade and msg1 (pairing_psk returns None). pair() then tries the next addr and the user sees pair_unreachable (Cannot reach host) for a host that was reached. G6(4) groups a wrong host key with PairAuthFailed. Consider PairAuthFailed or PairWindowClosed for /pair closes in msg1-sent.

refused is reset only by goLive; an Unreachable or Closed attempt between two LinkRefused does not reset it, nor does a network change, so two in a row means two since the last live link. A transient close in the msg1->msg2 window (indistinguishable from a KK refusal at the socket layer) counts. Keys stay stored either way, so nothing is lost.

goLive resets backoffIndex, so a host that sends welcome then closes each time (event queue overflow, kick) is redialled about every 1 s, held only by the 10 per minute gate, which sits exactly at the host per-source handshake limit. Consider resetting backoff only after the link has stayed up a while.

o.psk and the client secret hex stay in the connect closure for the life of the pair connection, which becomes the live link. JS strings cannot be wiped, and the psk is single-use once the window is consumed, so harmless. Verified: no key material in ControllerState, HostSummary, LinkFailure or the provider value.
